name: Waymo Training
from: Option 3: trolley-problem choices in a command line, revealed at the end as training data for self-driving cars.
hook: Ten quick ethics questions. Your answers will drive a car.
pitch: A green command-line survey of trolley problems, each answered with A or B. After the tenth, the reveal: the answers trained a fleet of self-driving cars. The second half replays your rules on a real street.
minute_check: Yes: the reveal is the pitch.
build_check: Yes: ten texts and one street replay.
scope: Ten scenarios, one replay street. The reveal is the whole game; make the first half feel harmless.

brief.player: Someone taking a short ethics survey in a terminal.
brief.fail: None. Every answer is accepted and stored.
brief.ending: The reveal: your answers trained the cars. The second half replays your choices as real street scenes with their consequences.
brief.theme: A split-second moral choice turned into a training weight. The player’s casual answers become rules.
brief.look: Green command line with an ASCII guide; then a more realistic, three-dimensional street.

prov.bug: Ten quick questions, then a twist!
prov.nit: Would the player answer differently if they knew? Should they get to answer again?

refs_lit: Awad et al., “The Moral Machine experiment” (Nature, 2018)
MIT’s real version: millions of people answered these scenarios online. Cite it; borrow its scenario format.
Philippa Foot, “The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of the Double Effect” (1967)
Where the trolley problem comes from.
The best-known twist where a training game turns out to have been real.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Dual-phase retro-terminal-to-3D simulation game: starts on a black phosphor CRT screen (#020a05) with glowing green (#46f28a) vector diagrams of a two-lane road junction, then seamlessly zooms through the glass into a stylized low-poly 3D night street bathed in green lidar scanlines where an autonomous car swerves cleanly between glowing pedestrian silhouettes according to the selected rule path. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for phosphor green terminal palette. Sound design: mechanical keyboard clack, modem tone morphing into electric vehicle hum and tires on wet asphalt. No dialogue.
